question: A combination of vehicles falls into Class A (Group A) when the gross combination weight rating (GCWR) is 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed is more than what weight?
choice_a: 10,000 pounds
choice_b: 5,000 pounds
choice_c: 15,000 pounds
choice_d: 26,001 pounds
explanation: The manual states a combination vehicle falls in Group A when GCWR is 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed is more than 10,000 pounds.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: Any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle not in excess of 10,000 pounds GVWR, falls into which class?
choice_a: Class C
choice_b: Class A
choice_c: Class B
choice_d: There is no CDL requirement for such a vehicle
explanation: The manual describes Class B (Group B) as any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle not exceeding 10,000 pounds GVWR.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: A single vehicle with a GVWR under 26,001 pounds falls into Class C and requires a CDL only if it meets which condition?
choice_a: It is designed to carry 16 or more passengers including the driver, or is used to transport hazardous materials requiring placarding
choice_b: It is more than 20 feet long
choice_c: It has more than two axles
choice_d: It is used exclusively for interstate commerce
explanation: The manual states Class C vehicles are included in the CDL program only if designed to carry 16 or more passengers including the driver, or used to transport hazardous materials in quantities requiring placarding (or carrying a select agent/toxin under 42 CFR part 73).
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: According to the manual, a driver who has qualified for a Class A license may also drive vehicles in which other classes?
choice_a: Classes B and C
choice_b: Class B only
choice_c: Class C only
choice_d: No other classes without additional testing
explanation: The manual explains that since Class A skills include those required for Class B and C vehicles, a driver with a Class A license may also drive vehicles in Classes B and C.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: A driver hauling material designated hazardous under 49 U.S.C. 5103 that is required to be placarded must add which endorsement to their CDL?
choice_a: Hazardous Materials (H)
choice_b: Tank Vehicle (N)
choice_c: Combination Hazardous Materials and Tank Vehicle (X)
choice_d: Passenger (P)
explanation: The manual states any driver hauling material designated hazardous and required to be placarded under 49 CFR part 172 must add a hazardous materials (H) endorsement and pass a special written examination on recognizing, handling, and transporting hazardous materials.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: A Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement is required for a tank with an individual rated capacity of more than how many gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of at least how many gallons?
choice_a: More than 119 gallons individual; 1,000 gallons or more aggregate
choice_b: More than 500 gallons individual; 2,000 gallons or more aggregate
choice_c: More than 50 gallons individual; 500 gallons or more aggregate
choice_d: More than 200 gallons individual; 1,500 gallons or more aggregate
explanation: The manual defines a tank vehicle requiring the N endorsement as one with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more that is attached to the vehicle or chassis.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: Why does the manual say a special knowledge examination is required for a driver to add the Doubles/Triples (T) endorsement?
choice_a: Considerable additional knowledge and skill is necessary to safely pull double or triple trailers in various traffic conditions
choice_b: Because federal law requires a background check for all combination vehicles
choice_c: Because it is only available to drivers with a Class C license
choice_d: Because double and triple trailers cannot be equipped with air brakes
explanation: The manual explains research shows considerable additional knowledge and skill is necessary to safely pull double or triple trailers, so Class A drivers who wish to do so must pass a special knowledge examination and add the T endorsement.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: The Passenger (P) endorsement is required for drivers of a vehicle with a design capacity to carry how many people, including the driver?
choice_a: 16 or more
choice_b: 8 or more
choice_c: 10 or more
choice_d: 24 or more
explanation: The manual states drivers who wish to drive a vehicle with a design capacity to carry 16 or more people, including the driver, must add a passenger (P) endorsement and pass a special knowledge examination plus a skills test in a passenger vehicle.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: Which endorsements, according to the manual, are the only ones that may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)?
choice_a: Passenger (P), School Bus (S), and Tank Vehicle (N)
choice_b: Hazardous Materials (H), Tank Vehicle (N), and Doubles/Triples (T)
choice_c: All six endorsements may be added to a CLP
choice_d: Passenger (P) and Hazardous Materials (H) only
explanation: The manual specifically notes that the only endorsements that may be added to a CLP are Passenger (P), School Bus (S), and Tank Vehicle (N).
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: Under restriction code L, what happens if an applicant does not take or fails the air brake component of the knowledge test, or takes the skills test in a vehicle without air brakes?
choice_a: They are restricted from operating a CMV equipped with any type of air brakes
choice_b: They must retake the entire knowledge test
choice_c: They are restricted only from operating tank vehicles
choice_d: They receive a K restriction instead
explanation: The manual states that under the L restriction, the state must indicate the person is restricted from operating a CMV equipped with any type of air brakes, including those operating fully or partially on the air brake principle.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: What does restriction code K indicate on a CDL?
choice_a: The person is restricted from operating a CMV in interstate commerce (intrastate only)
choice_b: The person cannot operate a vehicle with a manual transmission
choice_c: The person cannot operate a vehicle with air brakes
choice_d: The person is restricted from carrying passengers
explanation: The manual explains that if an applicant certifies status as Non-Excepted or Excepted Intrastate, the state indicates on the CDL that the person is restricted from operating a CMV in interstate commerce via the K restriction.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: If an applicant performs the skills test in a vehicle equipped with an automatic transmission, what restriction is placed on the CDL?
choice_a: E - No manual transmission
choice_b: L - No air brake equipped CMV
choice_c: O - No tractor trailer CMV
choice_d: Z - No full air brake equipped CMV
explanation: The manual states that if the skills test is performed in a vehicle with an automatic transmission, the state must indicate the person is restricted from operating a CMV with a manual transmission, using restriction code E.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: Which CDL knowledge test must be taken by all applicants, regardless of the class of license or endorsements sought?
choice_a: The general knowledge test
choice_b: The air brakes test
choice_c: The combination vehicles test
choice_d: The passenger transport test
explanation: The manual lists the general knowledge test as the test taken by all applicants, while the other knowledge tests (air brakes, combination vehicles, hazardous materials, tank vehicle, doubles/triples, school bus, passenger transport) apply only depending on the class or endorsement sought.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-5

question: The CDL Skills Test consists of three segments that must be taken in a specific order. What is that order?
choice_a: Vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, on-road driving
choice_b: On-road driving, vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control
choice_c: Basic vehicle control, on-road driving, vehicle inspection
choice_d: Vehicle inspection, on-road driving, basic vehicle control
explanation: The manual states the CDL Skills Test consists of vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, and on-road driving, and that applicants must take the segments in that order, passing each before moving to the next.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-5

question: During the vehicle inspection portion of the skills test, what is the applicant required to do?
choice_a: Point to/touch and name the item being inspected and explain to the examiner what would be inspected and why
choice_b: Only verbally list the items without touching the vehicle
choice_c: Complete a written checklist instead of a physical inspection
choice_d: Watch a video demonstration and answer questions about it
explanation: The manual states applicants must point to/touch and name the item being inspected and explain to the examiner what they would inspect and why.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-5

question: According to the manual, when is a CMV driver operating in interstate commerce?
choice_a: When driving from one state to another, or when a trip within a state crosses into another state or the cargo/passengers are part of a trip that began or ends in another state
choice_b: Only when the vehicle physically crosses a state line at some point on every single trip
choice_c: Whenever the driver holds a CDL issued by a different state than where they live
choice_d: Only when hauling hazardous materials across state lines
explanation: The manual defines interstate commerce as driving from one state to another or a foreign country, driving between two places within a state where part of the trip crosses into another state, or driving between two places within a state where the cargo or passengers are part of a trip beginning or ending in another state.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-6

question: A driver who operates in non-excepted interstate commerce is required to provide which document to their State Driver Licensing Agency (SDLA)?
choice_a: A current medical examiner's certificate (commonly called a medical certificate or DOT card)
choice_b: A copy of their vehicle's IRP registration
choice_c: An IFTA quarterly tax return
choice_d: A hazardous materials background check clearance letter
explanation: The manual states that drivers who operate in non-excepted interstate commerce are required to provide a current medical examiner's certificate, referred to as a medical certificate or DOT card, under 49 CFR 391.45.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: When completing a CDL application, how many self-certification statement categories describe a driver's operating status?
choice_a: Four (interstate non-excepted, interstate excepted, intrastate non-excepted, intrastate excepted)
choice_b: Two (interstate and intrastate only)
choice_c: Three (excepted, non-excepted, and exempt)
choice_d: Six, matching the six CDL endorsements
explanation: The manual lists four self-certification statement categories: interstate non-excepted, interstate excepted, intrastate non-excepted, and intrastate excepted.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: What happens if a driver who is required to have a 'certified' medical status fails to provide and keep up-to-date their medical examiner's certificate?
choice_a: The driver becomes 'not-certified' and may lose their CDL
choice_b: The driver is automatically issued a 90-day grace period with no consequence
choice_c: The driver's endorsement is downgraded but the CDL remains valid
choice_d: Nothing happens unless the driver is also convicted of a moving violation
explanation: The manual warns that a driver required to have a 'certified' medical status who fails to provide and keep up-to-date their medical examiner's certificate becomes 'not-certified' and may lose their CDL.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-6

question: For a first offense such as driving a CMV with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of .04% or higher, refusing alcohol testing, or leaving the scene of an accident involving a CMV, for how long will a driver lose their CDL, at a minimum?
choice_a: At least one year
choice_b: At least 30 days
choice_c: At least six months
choice_d: At least five years
explanation: The manual lists first-offense violations including BAC .04%+, DUI, refusing testing, leaving the scene of an accident, and committing a felony involving a CMV as resulting in loss of CDL for at least one year.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: If a disqualifying alcohol or controlled substance offense occurs while a driver is operating a CMV that is placarded for hazardous materials, how long will the driver lose their CDL at a minimum?
choice_a: At least three years
choice_b: At least one year
choice_c: At least six months
choice_d: For life, with no exceptions
explanation: The manual states a driver will lose their CDL for at least three years if the disqualifying offense occurs while operating a CMV placarded for hazardous materials.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: What penalty does the manual describe for a second offense of the listed disqualifying violations (such as DUI or driving a CMV with BAC .04% or higher)?
choice_a: Loss of CDL for life
choice_b: Loss of CDL for five years
choice_c: A fine only, with no loss of CDL
choice_d: Loss of CDL for three years
explanation: The manual states a driver will lose their CDL for life for a second offense of the listed disqualifying violations.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: A driver who commits two serious traffic violations within a three-year period involving a CMV will lose their CDL for how long, at a minimum?
choice_a: At least 60 days
choice_b: At least 30 days
choice_c: At least 120 days
choice_d: At least one year
explanation: The manual states a driver loses their CDL for at least 60 days for two serious traffic violations within a three-year period, and at least 120 days for three or more.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: For a first violation of a railroad-highway grade crossing rule, how long, at minimum, will a driver lose their CDL?
choice_a: At least 60 days
choice_b: At least 90 days
choice_c: At least 30 days
choice_d: At least one year
explanation: The manual states a driver will lose their CDL for at least 60 days for a first railroad-highway grade crossing violation, at least 120 days for a second within three years, and at least one year for a third within three years.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as a reason a driver would be denied or lose a hazardous materials endorsement?
choice_a: Being wanted or under indictment for certain felonies
choice_b: Having a Class C license instead of Class A
choice_c: Failing to renew vehicle registration on time
choice_d: Operating in excepted interstate commerce
explanation: The manual lists being wanted or under indictment for certain felonies, along with factors like not being a lawful permanent resident, renouncing U.S. citizenship, certain convictions, mental capacity adjudication, or being deemed a TSA security threat, as reasons an applicant will be denied or lose a hazardous materials endorsement.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: According to the manual's rules on distracted driving, what is a CDL holder prohibited from doing while driving?
choice_a: Holding a mobile telephone to conduct a voice communication or dialing it by pressing more than a single button, and sending or reading text messages
choice_b: Using a hands-free Bluetooth headset for any purpose
choice_c: Listening to the radio
choice_d: Speaking with a passenger in the vehicle
explanation: The manual states drivers are not allowed to hold a mobile telephone to conduct a voice communication or dial it by pressing more than a single button, and are not allowed to send or read text messages while driving.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-9

question: What does the manual say about a CDL holder possessing more than one driver's license?
choice_a: It is not allowed; a court may fine the driver up to $5,000 or jail them, and only the home state license is kept
choice_b: It is allowed as long as both licenses are CDLs
choice_c: It is allowed only if one license is a CLP
choice_d: It is allowed if the driver notifies their employer
explanation: The manual states a CDL holder cannot have more than one license; breaking this rule can result in a court fine of up to $5,000 or jail, with the driver's home state license kept and any others returned.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-9

question: Under the International Registration Plan (IRP), a Qualified Vehicle used for transporting persons for hire or property generally meets the definition if it has two axles and a gross vehicle weight or registered gross vehicle weight in excess of what amount, or has three or more axles regardless of weight?
choice_a: 26,000 pounds
choice_b: 10,000 pounds
choice_c: 80,000 pounds
choice_d: 33,000 pounds
explanation: The manual defines a Qualified Vehicle under the IRP as having two axles and a gross vehicle weight or registered gross vehicle weight in excess of 26,000 pounds, or three or more axles regardless of weight, or being used in a combination exceeding 26,000 pounds.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-10
